what_its_for: Lomitapide is used to lower very high levels of bad cholesterol (LDL cholesterol) in adults who have a rare inherited condition called Homozygous Familial Hypercholesterolemia (HoFH). This condition causes dangerously high cholesterol from birth and greatly increases the risk of heart disease. Lomitapide is used along with a low-fat diet and other cholesterol-lowering medicines.
how_to_take: Take lomitapide by mouth once a day, in the evening, at least 2 hours after your evening meal. Swallow the capsule whole — do not open, crush, or chew it. Taking it with food can cause more stomach side effects. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember. You must also follow a very low-fat diet (less than 20% of calories from fat) while taking this medicine to reduce stomach problems.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose (usually 5 mg once daily) and slowly increase it over several weeks to months, based on how well you tolerate it and how much your cholesterol levels improve. The maximum dose is 60 mg per day. Never change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip it and take your next dose the following evening as usual. Do not take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store lomitapide capsules at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep them away from heat, moisture, and light. Store them in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking grapefruit juice or eating grapefruit while taking lomitapide, as it can increase the amount of medicine in your blood and raise your risk of side effects. Avoid drinking alcohol — it can increase the risk of serious liver damage. Avoid eating high-fat meals, as fat increases stomach side effects like diarrhea and nausea. Tell your doctor about ALL medicines you take, including vitamins and herbal supplements, because many medications can interact with lomitapide, especially blood thinners (like warfarin), birth control pills, and certain antibiotics or antifungal medicines.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you experience: yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, severe stomach pain, nausea or vomiting that won't stop, unusual tiredness or weakness, or signs of liver problems. Also call your doctor if you have ongoing diarrhea, significant weight loss, or if you become pregnant while taking this medicine. Lomitapide can harm an unborn baby, so women who can become pregnant must use effective birth control while taking it.
when_it_works: Lomitapide starts working within a few weeks, but it may take several months of gradual dose increases to reach the full effect on your cholesterol levels. Your doctor will do regular blood tests to check your cholesterol and liver function throughout your treatment. This medicine controls your cholesterol but does not cure your condition, so it is important to keep taking it as prescribed.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Lomitapide can cause serious harm to an unborn baby. Women who can become pregnant must use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 2 weeks after stopping. Do not take lomitapide if you are pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if lomitapide passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Liver disease: Do not take lomitapide if you have active liver disease or persistently high liver enzyme levels. Your doctor will monitor your liver with blood tests regularly. Kidney disease: Use with caution if you have kidney disease or are on dialysis — your doctor may need to adjust your dose. Children: Lomitapide is only approved for use in adults 18 years and older.
